# `write-short`

Caps the length of each **logical comment**.

A logical comment is:

- a run of `//` comments on adjacent lines (blank lines, code, and directives break the run);
- a `/* ... */` block comment;
- one prose section of a JSDoc block — the description, or one tag's description. Tag names,
  `{type}` annotations, and parameter names never count.

The limit measures prose, not formatting: reformatting a comment, or wrapping it across lines,
never changes its length.

Tooling directives (`eslint-disable*`, `@ts-expect-error`, `biome-ignore`, `prettier-ignore`,
coverage and bundler pragmas, and similar) stay exempt. The rule lints the justification a
directive carries as prose.

The rule provides no autofix: shortening prose is a writing decision, not a mechanical one.

## Options

Either a single number, applied to every comment kind:

```js
'comment-slop/write-short': ['warn', 120]
```

Or an object with per-kind limits; omitted kinds default to `80`, and `false` disables a kind:

```js
'comment-slop/write-short': ['warn', { line: 80, block: 120, jsdoc: false }]
```

| Option             | Type              | Default              | Description                                                                |
| :----------------- | :---------------- | :------------------- | :------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `line`             | `number \| false` | `80`                 | Limit for `//` comments, including merged runs of adjacent lines.          |
| `block`            | `number \| false` | `80`                 | Limit for `/* ... */` comments that are not JSDoc.                         |
| `jsdoc`            | `number \| false` | `80`                 | Limit for each prose section of a `/** ... */` block.                      |
| `jsdocIgnoredTags` | `string[]`        | `['example', 'see']` | JSDoc tags whose sections the rule never checks. Replaces the default set. |

## Examples

### Logical comments

Comment length is judged per logical comment: a run of adjacent `//` lines, a block comment, or one JSDoc prose section. The prose is normalized (markers, `*` gutters, and repeated whitespace stripped) before counting, and the default limit is 80 characters.

The following patterns are considered problems:

```js
// Completed tasks are kept for thirty days so that the user can always restore them from the archive view.
// "comment-slop/write-short": ["error"]
// Message: line comment is 104 characters (max 80).
```

```js
// Tasks are soft-deleted first and only purged by the nightly cleanup job
// so that an accidental swipe can always be undone from the trash screen
moveToTrash(task)
// "comment-slop/write-short": ["error"]
// Message: line comment is 142 characters (max 80).
```

```js
/*
 * Reminders fire through the notification service rather than a local timer, so they still arrive when the app is closed.
 */
// "comment-slop/write-short": ["error"]
// Message: block comment is 119 characters (max 80).
```

```js
/**
 * Builds the list of tasks shown on the Today screen, including overdue items carried over from previous days.
 * @param dueDate - The due date in the timezone the task was created in, which may differ from the timezone of the current device.
 */
function todayList(dueDate) {
  return dueDate
}
// "comment-slop/write-short": ["error"]
// Message: JSDoc description is 108 characters (max 80).
// Message: JSDoc @param "dueDate" description is 113 characters (max 80).
```

```js
completeTask(task) // Completed tasks are kept for thirty days so that the user can always restore them from the archive view.
// "comment-slop/write-short": ["error"]
// Message: line comment is 104 characters (max 80).
```

```js
/**
 * Schedules a reminder.
 * @param dueDate - The due date in the timezone the task was created in, which may differ from the timezone of the current device.
 */
function schedule(dueDate) {
  return dueDate
}
// "comment-slop/write-short": ["error"]
// Message: JSDoc @param "dueDate" description is 113 characters (max 80).
```

The following patterns are not considered problems:

```js

// "comment-slop/write-short": ["error"]
```

```js

// "comment-slop/write-short": ["error"]
```

```js

// "comment-slop/write-short": ["error"]
```

```js
const overdue = tasks.filter(isOverdue)
// "comment-slop/write-short": ["error"]
```

```js

// Reminders are scheduled when the task is saved
// "comment-slop/write-short": ["error"]
```

```js

// Reminders are scheduled when the task is saved
// "comment-slop/write-short": ["error"]
```

```js
//    Snoozed     tasks     reappear     at     the     start     of     the     next     day
// "comment-slop/write-short": ["error"]
```

```js

  return tasksScheduledForToday
}
// "comment-slop/write-short": ["error"]
```

### Directives and justifications

Tooling directives are exempt from length limits — a long rule list is not prose. When a directive carries a justification (after `--` for ESLint, after `:` for Biome, trailing text for `@ts-expect-error`), the justification alone is linted, under the limit of the comment kind that contains it.

The following patterns are considered problems:

```js
// eslint-disable-next-line no-param-reassign -- the drag handler mutates DOM nodes directly because the task list is virtualised and re-renders on every frame
task.order = index
// "comment-slop/write-short": ["error"]
// Message: directive justification is 110 characters (max 80).
```

```js
/* eslint-disable no-param-reassign -- the drag handler mutates DOM nodes directly because the task list is virtualised and re-renders on every frame */
// "comment-slop/write-short": ["error"]
// Message: directive justification is 110 characters (max 80).
```

```js
// @ts-expect-error the drag handler mutates DOM nodes directly because the task list is virtualised and re-renders on every frame
const order = task.order
// "comment-slop/write-short": ["error"]
// Message: directive justification is 110 characters (max 80).
```

```js
// biome-ignore lint/suspicious/noExplicitAny: the drag handler mutates DOM nodes directly because the task list is virtualised and re-renders on every frame
const order = task.order
// "comment-slop/write-short": ["error"]
// Message: directive justification is 110 characters (max 80).
```

```js
// Completed tasks are kept for thirty days so that the user can always restore them from the archive view.
// eslint-disable-next-line no-console
// Reminders fire through the notification service rather than a local timer, so they still arrive when the app is closed.

// "comment-slop/write-short": ["error"]
// Message: line comment is 104 characters (max 80).
// Message: line comment is 119 characters (max 80).
```

```js

// "comment-slop/write-short": ["error"]
```


### Ignored JSDoc tags

JSDoc tags whose content is a reference or code rather than prose are exempt: `@see` and `@example` by default. The `jsdocIgnoredTags` option replaces the default set.

The following patterns are considered problems:

```js
/**
 * @see https://example.com/docs/tasks/recurrence-rules-and-timezone-handling-for-scheduled-reminders
 */
// "comment-slop/write-short": ["error",{"jsdocIgnoredTags":[]}]
// Message: JSDoc @see description is 93 characters (max 80).
```

```js
/**
 * @see https://example.com/docs/tasks/recurrence-rules-and-timezone-handling-for-scheduled-reminders
 */
// "comment-slop/write-short": ["error",{"jsdocIgnoredTags":["todo"]}]
// Message: JSDoc @see description is 93 characters (max 80).
```

The following patterns are not considered problems:

```js
/**
 * @see https://example.com/docs/tasks/recurrence-rules-and-timezone-handling-for-scheduled-reminders
 */
// "comment-slop/write-short": ["error"]
```

```js
/**
 * @example
 * addTask("Water the plants", { due: "tomorrow", repeat: "weekly" })
 * addTask("File taxes", { due: "2026-04-15", remind: "1 week before" })
 */
// "comment-slop/write-short": ["error"]
```

```js
/**
 * @todo Reminders fire through the notification service rather than a local timer, so they still arrive when the app is closed.
 */
// "comment-slop/write-short": ["error",{"jsdocIgnoredTags":["todo"]}]
```

### Options

The option is either a single number applied to every kind, or an object with per-kind limits (`line`, `block`, `jsdoc`). Omitted kinds fall back to the default of 80; `false` disables a kind entirely.

The following patterns are considered problems:

```js
// snooze it
/* snooze it */
/** Snooze it. */
// "comment-slop/write-short": ["error",8]
// Message: line comment is 9 characters (max 8).
// Message: block comment is 9 characters (max 8).
// Message: JSDoc description is 10 characters (max 8).
```

```js
// remind the user before the due date
/* due soon */
// "comment-slop/write-short": ["error",{"block":40,"line":10}]
// Message: line comment is 35 characters (max 10).
```

```js
// Completed tasks are kept for thirty days so that the user can always restore them from the archive view.
// "comment-slop/write-short": ["error",{"jsdoc":200}]
// Message: line comment is 104 characters (max 80).
```

```js
// eslint-disable-next-line no-console -- surfaced in the debug panel
console.log(task)
// "comment-slop/write-short": ["error",{"line":10}]
// Message: directive justification is 27 characters (max 10).
```

The following patterns are not considered problems:

```js
// Completed tasks are kept for thirty days so that the user can always restore them from the archive view.
// "comment-slop/write-short": ["error",{"line":false}]
```

```js
/** Builds the list of tasks shown on the Today screen, including overdue items carried over from previous days. */
// "comment-slop/write-short": ["error",{"jsdoc":200}]
```

```js
// Completed tasks are kept for thirty days so that the user can always restore them from the archive view.
// "comment-slop/write-short": ["error",104]
```
